sites.rationale: L2 explicitly names junction 23/24 (PAins1) in the N-terminal PSI domain segment of full-length membrane-anchored β7. Python confirms residue 23 = A and residue 24 = K in the canonical human sequence; both are extracellular (landmarks: EC 20–725) and >700 residues from the TM boundary. L3 confirms surface display by flow cytometry for all four insertion mutants including PAins1; ranked below PAins2 because the Mn2+-dependent conformational readout is not separately reported for this junction. Full-length murine β7 integrin expressed in β7-KO BAF cells via pcDNA3.1 construct; PA tag inserted between residues 23 and 24 (PAins1) by inverse PCR; surface display confirmed by NZ-1 (anti-PA) and FIB504 (anti-β7) flow cytometry in the presence of Ca2+/Mg2+ or Mn2+.

literature_notes: All four sites derive from a single paper (PMC7413538) reporting PA-tag knock-ins into full-length murine β7 integrin expressed in β7-KO BAF cells. The paper explicitly names all four junctions (PAins1–4) and confirms surface display for all by flow cytometry (L2, L3). PAins2 (29/30) receives the highest validation because L4 demonstrates Mn2+-dependent 8-fold increase in NZ-1 binding, proving conformational regulation is preserved. PAins1 (23/24) and PAins2 (29/30) are in the N-terminal PSI domain segment (residues ~20–65); PAins3 (427/428) and PAins4 (431/432) are in the C-terminal PSI domain segment (~427–470), which re-associates with the N-terminal segment in the folded integrin. PAins3 is ranked lowest because C428 (a PSI-domain disulfide cysteine) is the immediate residue after the junction, introducing structural risk not present at the other three sites. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions were reported in the ledger for ITGB7.
